mechanism: unicode61 splits on non-alphanumerics and lowercases, so get_user_by_id / get-user-by-id / user.get.by.id / GET_USER_BY_ID all index as the separate tokens a natural-language query produces, while getUserById / GetUserById / GetUserByID index as one opaque token sharing no term with that query. The extractor cannot help: it lowercases before splitting and splits only on _, - and /, never on case.
reading: Arm prose_rich shows the cost is ZERO for reach when a natural comment is present -- English prose carries the chunk. The identifier-only and prose-shared arms isolate what the comment was hiding.
why_it_matters: MULocBench (108k genes, delivered .449) is the only code bed and is Python-heavy. Any camelCase corpus (Java, JS/TS, Go, C#) inherits whatever gap these arms measure, for a reason no ranking change can reach -- it is upstream of every lane.
scope_limits: Closed synthetic corpus (8 gold + 10 siblings per arm): measures tokenizer behaviour, not ranking on a real bed.
Says nothing about how often real code queries are natural language versus pasted identifiers -- a real code bed answers that.
Comment density is the hidden variable: prose_rich is the well-commented extreme, identifier_only the uncommented extreme. Real corpora sit between them.
BM25 ranking over 18 documents is not the shipped funnel; the rank columns show separation, not delivered position.
